title: Kelvin–Helmholtz billows
alt: Two horizontal shear layers on black roll up into rows of spiral vortices, the upper row red (negative vorticity), the lower row green (positive), trailing thin filaments that wrap around each core.
caption: Vorticity of two tanh shear layers (half-thickness δ = 0.08, Re = Uδ/ν = 400), nonlinear IVP seeded by the box mode nearest the most unstable one (αδ = 0.503); t = 3 to 9, one frame every 0.025 time units, played at 0.6 time units per second. 384 × 192 RealFourier modes (3/2 dealiasing), streamfunction form, RK443, dt = 0.0025, CPU.
field: Vorticity ω = −∇²ψ (normal to the plane) of two shear layers rolling up, t = 3 to 9.
colour: Colour: ω, red for negative, black at zero, glass green for positive; one scale for the whole film, ending at the 99.7th percentile of |ω| over all frames (10.8; larger values saturate).
extent: Periodic box 4 × 2 (x × z, lengths in units of the layer velocity scale), the full box.
measured: Growth rate of the seeded mode 2.05 (times δ: 0.164), fitted for t between 0.7 and 2.9.

film.loop: fade from black over the first 7 frames and to black over the last 7 (the end state is not the start state)
film.span: Simulated time 3 to 9, shown in 10.042 s of playback.

title: Kelvin–Helmholtz dye
alt: A pale horizontal band of passive dye between two shear layers; its edges curl into rows of spirals that entrain dark fluid, outlined by one thin fluorescent yellow-green line at half concentration.
caption: Passive dye marking the central band (Schmidt number 1) in the same Kelvin–Helmholtz run, t = 3 to 9, one frame every 0.025, played at 0.6 time units per second; the line is the iso-concentration c = 1/2. 384 × 192 RealFourier modes (3/2 dealiasing), streamfunction form, RK443, dt = 0.0025, CPU.
field: Concentration c of a passive dye that starts as the central band, t = 3 to 9; the yellow-green line is c = 1/2.
colour: Colour: c, from 0 (black) to 1 (light grey), the same for every frame.
extent: Periodic box 4 × 2 (x × z), the full box.
measured: Growth rate of the seeded mode 2.05 (times δ: 0.164), fitted for t between 0.7 and 2.9.

title: Rayleigh–Bénard convection
alt: A long slab of convecting fluid on black: bright hot plumes rise from the bottom wall and dark cold plumes sink from the top, swept sideways by large convection rolls.
caption: Temperature in 2D Rayleigh–Bénard convection at Ra = 1e6, Pr = 1, aspect ratio 4, rigid walls, from seeded noise; t = 0.0312 to 0.0600 thermal times (29 free-fall times), one frame every 0.00012 thermal times, played at 2.9 free-fall times per second. 384 × 96 RealFourier × Chebyshev, 3/2 dealiasing, RK443, dt = 1e-05, CPU.
field: Temperature T (conduction profile included) of 2D convection at Ra = 10⁶, t = 0.0312 to 0.0600 thermal times (29 free-fall times).
colour: Colour: T, from −A (black) to +A (light grey), A = 0.315 the 99th percentile of |T| in the interior |z| < 0.4 over all frames; the boundary layers, which reach ±1/2, saturate.
extent: Box 4 × 1 (x × z), periodic in x, walls at z = ±1/2; lengths in units of the layer depth.
measured: Nusselt number 8.21 (volume), 8.1 (bottom wall), 8.15 (top wall), averaged for t between 0.031 and 0.06: a short window of one run, not a converged mean.

title: Kuramoto–Sivashinsky chaos, L = 22
alt: A space-time diagram scrolling to the left: wavy red and green stripes of negative and positive u merge, split and drift, separated by black zero lines, new time entering on the right.
caption: u(x, t) of u_t + u u_x + u_xx + u_xxxx = 0 on a periodic domain L = 22 after a transient of 300; the 125-unit window scrolls by 250 time units, played at 25 time units per second. RealFourier N = 32 (dealias 3/2), RK443, dt = 0.01.
field: The solution u(x, t) of the Kuramoto–Sivashinsky equation, L = 22, in a window of 125 time units that moves from t = 300–425 to t = 550–675: x upwards, t to the right.
colour: Colour: u, red for negative, black at zero, glass green for positive; the scale ends at the 99.7th percentile of |u| over the whole run shown (2.71).
extent: x from 0 to 22 (periodic) upwards; 125 time units across the frame.
measured: Energy over the window: mean 0.7084, between 0.4213 and 1.445; spatial mean of u at most 3.6e−15.

title: Taylor–Couette: the first Taylor vortices
alt: A horizontal band between two cylinder walls, dark at first, where alternating red and green vertical stripes of azimuthal velocity grow and brighten, circled by thin silver streamlines of the Taylor vortices.
caption: Taylor vortices growing between rotating cylinders, radius ratio η = 0.5, outer cylinder at rest, at Re = 80 (1.17 times the onset value 68.19 of the still) from a small seeded axisymmetric perturbation, t = 89.95 to 210 (time unit: gap / inner wall speed), played at 12 time units per second. The still shows the critical mode, which is steady; the film is a nonlinear run above onset. Native model conatus.problems.taylor_couette, Fourier × Chebyshev × Fourier 4 × 24 × 32, RK443, dt = 0.005, CPU.
field: Azimuthal velocity perturbation u_φ in the meridional (z, r) plane, with streamlines of the meridional flow (u_r, u_z), as Taylor vortices grow at Re = 80 from t = 89.95 to 210.
colour: Colour: u_φ − V(r), red for negative, black at zero, glass green for positive; one scale for the film, the largest |u_φ − V| over all frames (0.173, in units of the inner wall speed). Streamlines at fixed levels of the largest stream function over the film, so they appear as the vortices grow.
extent: Gap r_i ≤ r ≤ r_o (outer wall at the top) over the axial period, two wavelengths 2π/k, k = 3.1625.
measured: Growth rate of the vortices 0.0581, fitted on the energy after the initial transient, up to 10 % of the saturated amplitude; the eigenvalue problem of the still's script gives 0.0588 at the same Re and k.

title: Swift–Hohenberg labyrinth
alt: Light and dark stripes appear out of an even grey, curve into a dense labyrinth of fixed width and slowly straighten into patches of parallel rolls that meet at defects.
caption: Rolls of du/dt = r u − (1 + ∇²)² u − u³ at r = 0.1 growing from noise in a periodic box of 24 × 12 roll wavelengths, t = 0 to 600, one frame every 2.5, played at 60 time units per second. RealFourier × RealFourier 192 × 96 (dealias 2 for the cubic term), SBDF2, dt = 0.5.
field: The field u(x, y) of the Swift–Hohenberg equation at r = 0.1, from seeded noise at t = 0 to t = 600.
colour: Colour: u, from −0.502 (black, troughs) to +0.502 (light grey, crests), the largest |u| of the final state; the same scale for every frame, so the small initial noise is grey.
extent: Periodic box of 24 × 12 roll wavelengths (2π each), the full box.
measured: r.m.s. of u 0.2466 (straight rolls: 0.2583); largest |∂u/∂t| 0.0043 at the last step.

title: Rossby–Haurwitz wave on the sphere
alt: A globe seen from mid-northern latitudes on black, covered by large alternating green and red vorticity lobes, four around each hemisphere, travelling east.
caption: Relative vorticity of the wavenumber-4 Rossby–Haurwitz wave (Williamson et al. 1992, test case 6), inviscid shallow water on the rotating sphere, over one period of the wave (7.97 days) from day 14.2, played at 0.8 days per second. The pattern returns after one period but the faint small-scale ripples do not: the last 7 frames are cross-faded into the first. Fourier × spin-weighted spherical harmonics, T63 (128 × 64), implicit Coriolis, RK443, dt = 0.03/Ω.
field: Relative vorticity ζ of the wavenumber-4 Rossby–Haurwitz wave over one period of the wave (7.97 days, from day 14.2), seen from 35° N by a fixed camera.
colour: Colour: ζ, red for negative, black at zero, glass green for positive; one scale for the film, the largest |ζ| over all frames (1.29, in units of Ω).
extent: The whole visible hemisphere of the unit sphere, orthographic projection.
measured: Period of the wave 7.966 days, from the turn of the m = 4 phase of the vorticity at 45° N; largest |ζ| over the film 1.291.

film.loop: one period of the wave (m = 4 phase measured); the last 7 frames are cross-faded with the same view one period earlier (the small-scale ripples differ)
film.span: Simulated time 89.67 to 139.7, shown in 9.958 s of playback.

title: Tollmien–Schlichting wave in a channel
alt: A wide band of red and green lobes on black sliding steadily to the right: the streamwise velocity of the least stable wave of plane channel flow, strongest just inside the top and bottom walls.
caption: Streamwise velocity of the Orr–Sommerfeld mode of plane Poiseuille flow at Re = 10000, α = 1, c = 0.23752649 + 0.00373967i, travelling at c_r over one period (26.45 time units in 10 s; the loop closes exactly). The time dependence is the mode's own exp(−iαct) without its growth factor. Chebyshev N = 64, dense QZ, tau modes removed by an N = 96 drift test.
field: Streamwise velocity perturbation Re(û(y) e^(iα(x − c_r t))) of the least stable Orr–Sommerfeld mode, over one period 2π/(α c_r) = 26.45 (the wave moves one wavelength).
colour: Colour: u normalised to a largest |û| of 1, red for negative, black at zero, glass green for positive; the slow growth exp(α c_i t) is left out, so the amplitude is the same in every frame.
extent: One wavelength 2π/α in x (to the right), the channel −1 ≤ y ≤ 1 (upwards), true aspect ratio.
measured: c = 0.237526489 + 0.00373967062i, eigenvector residual 1.4e−16, relative wall defect 1.5e−12.

film.loop: one period of the travelling wave: the frame after the last is the first (no transition)
